titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 10/2010 (ލޯކަލް ކައުންސިލްތަކުގެ އިންތިޚާބުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This short bill amends the Local Council Elections Act (Law 10/2010). It has three clauses: clause 1 replaces paragraph (c) of Article 9, clause 2 changes Article 26-1, and clause 3 says when the amendment takes effect. Both changes deal with how a vacant local council seat is handled, and they refer to Articles 15, 29 and 45 of the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010), which a companion bill also amends. Time periods of 183 days and 120 days are printed in clause 2. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: It appears to change the timing rules for filling empty local council seats, which affects residents of islands and cities who are waiting on a by-election and the Elections Commission's schedule.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 replaces paragraph (c) of Article 9. The new text refers to Article 26-1, but the full wording is not clear enough in the scan to state the rule.
Clause 2 amends Article 26-1 and adds references to Articles 15, 29 and 45 of the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010), the same articles amended by the companion bill.
Clause 2 also adds a new paragraph that mentions 183 days and 120 days. The scan does not make clear how the two periods work together.
Clause 3 sets when the amendment takes effect. It appears to be on publication in the government gazette after ratification, but the wording is partly unclear.
A comparison table at the back sets the old and new text of Articles 9(c) and 26-1 side by side. It is printed sideways and could not be read reliably.
whoIsAffected: Local council members, voters in councils with a vacant seat, and the Elections Commission.
statedReasons: The note says the bill is brought so the Local Council Elections Act matches a separate bill amending the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010), and it mentions periods of 183 and 120 days for council seats. The exact wording was hard to read.
